claim: Escontrela et al. (IROS 2022) demonstrated that AMP style rewards learned from a few seconds of motion capture data (German Shepherd) are sufficient to train a quadrupedal robot policy that transfers to real hardware.
stance_target: Minimal AMP demo dataset size for legged robot locomotion
scope_conditions: Quadrupedal robot, motion capture from German Shepherd, sim-to-real transfer
quoted_support: 'an effective style reward can be learned from a few seconds of motion capture data gathered from a German Shepherd and leads to energy-efficient locomotion strategies with natural gait transitions.'

claim: AMP policies trained from motion capture data exhibit energy efficiency (lower Cost of Transport) compared to policies trained with complex hand-designed reward functions.
stance_target: AMP energy efficiency advantage over reward engineering
quoted_support: 'A policy trained using AMP successfully tracks the desired forward velocity commands while exhibiting a lower COT than competing baselines... The energy efficiency of policies trained with AMP can likely be attributed to the policy extracting energy-efficient motion priors from the reference data.'

claim: AMP enables automatic gait transitions (e.g. pacing to canter) when velocity commands jump, analogous to how animals naturally transition gaits for energy efficiency.
stance_target: AMP naturalistic gait emergence for legged robots
quoted_support: 'The robot transitioning from a pacing motion to a canter motion when the desired velocity jumps from 1 m/s to 2 m/s. While pacing is the optimal gait at low speeds, entering a canter motion with a flight phase is a more energy-efficient option at high speeds.'
